$comment: Registry of every gate exemption in this repository. Consumed by
scripts/tests/test_gate_exemption_registry.py.
MEMBERSHIP IS DERIVED, REASONS ARE AUTHORED. scripts/exemption_discovery.py finds
every exemption surface in the tree -- Python constants by name AND by the prose of
their attached comment, Make variables, shell variables, linter config keys and JSON
baselines -- and the meta-test fails in BOTH directions: a surface that is not
registered here, and an entry here whose surface has vanished. This file is itself a
list, and the whole subject of the change that created it is that hand-maintained
lists go stale, so only the judgement in it is hand-maintained.
WHY IT EXISTS. Four exemption lists stated a premise that was false for at least one
member, and in each case the false member was the one the gate most needed to see.
Every one was the same bug: ONE justification attached to a SET, where the
justification is a property of individual members. Read in aggregate -- 'does this
reason hold broadly?' -- all four pass. So the rule this registry encodes is that a
reason answers for one member, and a premise that can be computed is computed.
FIELDS.
kind      exemption        a real carve-out: members escape an assertion
enforced-universe the list IS the enforced set; the risk is omission
prune             build output / gitignored local work, not a carve-out
fixture           test data that matched the vocabulary; turns nothing off
capability        a runtime allow/deny grant, not a gate
turnsOff  what stops being asserted for a member (required, non-empty)
premise   the name of a predicate in scripts/tests/gate_premises.py that the owning
gate evaluates PER MEMBER, or JUDGEMENT when there is genuinely nothing to
compute. JUDGEMENT is not an escape from scrutiny: a reason is then
required, and the ratchets still apply.
reason    required when premise is JUDGEMENT
ratchet   what makes the exemption finite even where the premise cannot be checked:
non-vacuity (it must shield something), count-pinned (it shields only as
many sites as were audited), universe-closure (nothing may sit outside
both sets), staleness (a dead entry fails), prune-meta-test (deferred to
test_repo_walk_guards_prune_local_work.py), or none
ratchetGap required when ratchet is none: what is consequently unprotected. These
are the honest residuals of this mechanism, and they are enumerable --
which is the point. An unmeasured gap is how this class started.
crossReferences  other entries that must be audited with this one. Two exemptions
pointed at each other in comments and two independent surveys audited one
half and never followed the pointer.
premiseWiring  'pending' on an entry whose premise IS computable but whose gate
does not yet call the predicate. It requires a reason and is counted:
MAX_PENDING_WIRING in the meta-test may shrink and not grow. This state
exists so that 'computable but unchecked' is distinguishable from
'nothing to compute' -- collapsing the two into JUDGEMENT is how a
checkable premise stops being checked.
predicateConsidered  {predicate: why it does not settle the question}. Required when
a JUDGEMENT reason invokes the subject of a predicate that exists --
nested stacks, the publisher's build, an installer manifest, test
collection. See the LIMIT below for what this does and does not buy.
THE LIMIT OF JUDGEMENT AND ratchetGap, STATED PLAINLY.
Both are escape hatches, and a mechanism that pretends otherwise would be the defect
it is meant to fix. So, precisely what each is worth:
* A JUDGEMENT reason cannot be checked. No test reads a sentence. What IS checked is
narrower and is the failure mode that actually occurred four times: a reason that
RESTATES IN PROSE a fact this tree can compute. If the wording invokes a
predicate's subject, the entry must name that predicate or set it aside in
predicateConsidered with a sentence. That is a lint on this file, not a claim about
the world -- it never asks whether a template is a nested stack, only whether an
author who wrote 'nested stack' engaged with the predicate that answers it.
* An author can still write a premise the vocabulary does not recognise, and get
JUDGEMENT plus ratchetGap for it. Nothing here stops that, and nothing here
pretends to. The bound on it is quantitative rather than semantic:
MAX_UNRATCHETED and MAX_PENDING_WIRING may shrink and not grow, so the cost of
reaching for the hatch is a deliberate, visible edit to a pinned number in a test
-- which is a review moment, not a check.
* PREDICATE_DOMAIN_WORDING is therefore the thing to keep current. It is the only
part of this mechanism that degrades silently: a new predicate whose subject is
not listed there can be restated in prose with nothing objecting. Adding a
predicate to gate_premises.PREDICATES means adding its wording there too.
* What none of this covers: whether a JUDGEMENT reason is TRUE. That remains a
reviewer's job, and it is why every reason here is required to state a fact about
this tree rather than restate AWS behaviour from memory -- the rule
TRANSPORT_CONTROL_EXEMPT states in its own comment, generalised.
memberKind  What ONE member names: "path", "deployable path" (a CloudFormation
template or a Lambda source tree), "CloudFormation logical id", "Bedrock
model id", "make target", and so on. Required, and not inferred: it
decides which predicates can possibly apply. A "deployable path" exemption
may NOT be pure JUDGEMENT -- whether the parent deploys it and whether one
publish run builds it are computable, and all four original defects
asserted one of them in prose. The rule stops at deployable paths on
purpose: demanding the same of a documentation link-check exemption would
produce boilerplate nobody reads, and a registry that asks for judgement
on noise gets rubber-stamped.
issues    Optional. Issue or PR numbers already addressing this exemption, so a reader
can tell a known-and-tracked carve-out from an unexamined one. Absent means
'nobody is working on it', which is itself information.

Makefile::COVERAGE_CICD_SKIP.memberKind: the name of one registry tree in check_coverage_debt.TREES whose coverage report the CI coverage-producer step does not generate
Makefile::COVERAGE_CICD_SKIP.turnsOff: nothing, for the one member it has. It removes `idp_common` from the trees `make coverage-all-cicd` measures, because the CI step immediately before it -- `make test-cicd -C lib/idp_common_pkg` -- already writes that tree's report to the path `check_coverage_debt.LEGACY_IDP_COMMON_REPORT` names. The ratchet step after it runs `--require-all-trees`, which requires `idp_common` BY NAME like every other tree, so the coverage of this tree is enforced exactly as it was; what is skipped is the second measurement of it, not the check.
Makefile::COVERAGE_CICD_SKIP.reason: Discovered by name: the fragment `SKIP` is in the discovery vocabulary, and it matching here is the mechanism working rather than a false positive -- a variable that removes a tree from a coverage producer is exactly the shape this registry governs, whatever its intent. The judgement is bounded to one member because the variable holds one: `--skip idp_common`. Why it is JUDGEMENT rather than a computed premise: the fact that would have to be computed is 'an earlier step in the same CI job already wrote this tree's report', and that is a property of the ORDER of steps in two CI configuration files, not of a path or a file on disk, so none of the predicates in gate_premises.py can express it and a new one would have to parse and order both configs to answer for a single member. What makes the entry safe without that is the ratchet, and it is stronger than the premise would have been: `check-coverage-debt-cicd` passes `--require-all-trees`, whose required set is derived from `TREES` inside `check_coverage_debt.py` rather than written out anywhere a skip could be mirrored. So a tree named here and produced by nobody is not quietly unmeasured -- it is named in a refusal and the gate exits 2. TestRequireAllTreesIsDerivedFromTheRegistry in scripts/tests/test_coverage_debt.py asserts that closure, including against a tree invented by the test so the derivation cannot be satisfied by hardcoding today's names, and test_the_cicd_producer_skips_exactly_the_tree_CI_already_measured in the same file pins the membership of this variable to exactly `idp_common` and pins that the recipe still invokes the producer -- deleting the recipe body is a mutation this registry entry alone would not catch and that assertion does. The residual a reviewer should check is the one thing neither asserts: that the earlier CI step really still writes that report. It is not unprotected, it is protected one layer out -- if that step stops writing it, `--require-all-trees` fails naming `idp_common`, which is the loud direction.

Two things make this more than a note. The equality means a third code declared in degradation.py fails. benchmarks/tests/test_processing_issues_.memberKind: a ProcessingIssue `code` string that no service in this repository emits
benchmarks/tests/test_processing_issues_.turnsOff: nothing. It is the NEGATIVE CONTROL for the property #1378 is about: three codes nobody has written, fed through the real writer and reader to prove the recorder tallies on each issue's own values rather than recognising a list of known types. A member being in it is what makes it a test input, not what excuses it from anything.
benchmarks/tests/test_processing_issues_.reason: Discovered through the prose route, on a comment explaining that a recognition rule 'would let codes through' -- which reads to the matcher as an exemption rationale and is the exact opposite. The three members are chosen so that no rule a recorder might plausibly carry admits any of them: one has a real stage prefix so an exact-code allowlist rejects it, one has no prefix any service uses so a prefix rule rejects it, one has a stage that is not a pipeline stage. That spread is measured rather than guessed: a single invented code spelled extraction_... left a recorder filtering on startswith(('extraction_', 'assessment_', 'classification_')) passing the entire suite, which is this issue's own defect one level up. The ratchet is that each member is asserted ABSENT from the AST-derived universe of real codes, so if a service ever adopts one of these names the negative control stops being negative and the test fails rather than becoming vacuous; the file also asserts the derived universe is non-empty, because an empty parametrisation collects as a pytest SKIP with a green exit. Registered rather than reworded, because rewording a comment to slip past discovery is the failure this registry exists to prevent.

benchmarks/tests/test_processing_issues_.memberKind: the `stage` string of a ProcessingIssue, as declared in idp_common/document_failure.py
benchmarks/tests/test_processing_issues_.turnsOff: nothing in a gate. It names the processing-issue stages whose issues reach the section's DynamoDB record and NOT the section result.json that analyze.score_processing_issues reads, so the benchmark harness cannot see them. Membership is a fact about where the pipeline writes, not a decision to skip anything, and the test compares `STAGES - SITE_STAGES` against it for EQUALITY in both directions.
benchmarks/tests/test_processing_issues_.reason: rule_validation and postprocessing build their issues through document_failure.record_section_failure from handlers in patterns/unified/src/, after extraction and assessment have written the section result.json, and nothing rewrites that file afterwards. So a stage in this list is one the harness is structurally blind to, and the whole point of registering it is that the blindness is written down instead of discovered again -- #1378 is itself an instance of a check firing into a field nobody read. The closure is an equality with no authored inventory on either side: the left-hand set is every stage whose only ProcessingIssue construction is the document_failure pass-through, derived by AST, and the right is this list, so a sixth stage lands in the left and fails rather than being silently unread. What a reviewer should check is that the equality is real -- add a *_STAGE constant to document_failure.py and watch test_every_declared_stage_is_either_covered_or_a_named_boundary fail. The reason this is not an exemption is that there is no gate here for it to excuse: nothing in this repository asserts the harness sees every stage, because measurement says it does not, and an assertion to the contrary is the defect rather than the fix.

lib/idp_common_pkg/idp_common/metering_u.memberKind: (shipped bedrock pricing key, omitted prompt-cache metering unit) pair

predicateConsidered.file_absent_or_untracked: Matched only on the phrase 'is absent', which here describes membership of a Python list -- a model id absent from bedrock.client.CACHEPOINT_SUPPORTED_MODELS -- and not a path. Every file this entry names is tracked and present, and that membership question is computed per member by the owning test rather than restated in prose.

lib/idp_common_pkg/idp_common/metering_u.turnsOff: the unpriced report for ONE cache unit on ONE pricing entry, and only for a member whose priced_by_aws is false. Such a member's metering row is written as $0.00 rather than as a NULL cost, in both cost implementations (idp_common/reporting/save_reporting_data.py::_get_unit_cost and benchmarks/harness/lib.py::price_metering). A member whose priced_by_aws is TRUE turns nothing off: it records the basis for the pricing.yaml omission and is deliberately NOT shielded at runtime, so the unit is still reported. A cache unit absent from any bedrock entry this register does not name is reported.
lib/idp_common_pkg/idp_common/metering_u.reason: This replaced two entries in NON_CHARGEABLE_METERING_UNITS that declared the two cache units free for the whole 'bedrock' service. That was one justification attached to a set where the justification is a property of individual members: AWS prices a cache read at $0.625/MTok on Nova Premier and publishes no cache dimension for Claude 3 Haiku in any of 17 regions, so a service-wide reason is false for one of them whichever way it is written. Measured before the change: a million cache-read tokens and a million cache-write tokens on each of the eleven shipped entries that omit the units came back as exactly $0.00 from both implementations with no unpriced marker, while a key with no entry at all was reported -- so the entry axis was visible and the unit axis was not. Each member now names the price-list model it was read against and what that reading showed, and both halves of its premise are computed -- with a stated reach, because what the computation establishes is narrower than the member's prose. The price-list half computes whether AWS publishes a non-zero rate for the dimension on the model NAMED, and pins that name to the entry citing it by requiring the entry's own input and output rates to be ones AWS publishes for that model: measured, that pins 18 of the 21 members to exactly one model out of 141. It does NOT detect a basis that is simply false -- a fabricated member naming a rate-compatible model with the convenient cache answer passes every mechanical check, and that is what this registry's one-member's-worth-of-authored-reason discipline is for, since no test can read a sentence. The residual where the ambiguity could change a verdict rather than merely the name is measured and pinned for equality in EXPECTED_RATE_AMBIGUOUS_IDENTITIES: one member today. The price-list half is asserted against a committed digest of AWS's two public offer files (bedrock_cache_dimension_digest.py, unauthenticated, refreshable with --refresh); priced_by_aws must equal whether that digest carries a non-zero rate, in both directions, and the digest's retrieval date must equal the date metering_units records. The reachability half -- that this code path can never meter the unit for the model, because the id is absent from bedrock.client.CACHEPOINT_SUPPORTED_MODELS and is not one of prompt_cache._IMPLICIT_CACHE_BASE_NAMES -- is asserted per member against those two constants, with both import targets probed first so a renamed or emptied list cannot make it pass vacuously. The premise is labelled JUDGEMENT rather than naming a gate_premises predicate because neither computation is a fact about this tree: one is a reading of a third party's published price list and the other spans two modules of the library under test, and a predicate takes one member and answers about the repository. Universe closure rather than a pinned count: the member set is DERIVED from config_library/pricing.yaml and asserted equal in both directions, so a twelfth entry omitting a cache rate fails for being unregistered and a member whose entry has since gained the rate fails for being stale. A count would be redundant beside that, and would turn paying the debt down -- adding a rate and deleting the member -- into a red gate. Non-vacuity is covered by the same closure plus a floor on the number of bedrock entries the YAML walk reads, which is deliberately NOT a floor on the number omitting: an empty derived list makes every parametrised assertion collect as a pytest skip, which reads green and proves nothing.

lib/idp_common_pkg/idp_common/metering_u.memberKind: metering unit, scoped to the leading component of a pricing key (the service)
lib/idp_common_pkg/idp_common/metering_u.turnsOff: the unpriced report for one (service, unit) pair. A pricing entry for that service may omit the unit and the metering row is written as $0.00 rather than as a NULL cost, in both cost implementations (idp_common/reporting/save_reporting_data.py::_get_unit_cost and benchmarks/harness/lib.py::price_metering). Every other absent unit with a non-zero count is reported.
lib/idp_common_pkg/idp_common/metering_u.reason: Four entries, each carrying its own sourcing rather than sharing one, because whether a unit is a billing dimension is a property of the unit and the service. Three cite AWS's public Bedrock price list by URL and say what it showed; the owning test re-asserts those against a committed digest of that file, derived by bedrock_price_list_digest.py, and re-derives it live under CHECK_AWS_PRICE_LIST=1. That is a computed premise, but the computation is a reading of a published price list rather than a fact about this tree, so there is no gate_premises predicate for it and the entry says JUDGEMENT instead of naming one it does not call. One entry is a judgement outright and labelled so: 'requests' on a LambdaHook is a counter this project injects for shape parity with a Bedrock response, not a third party's billing dimension, so no price list settles it. It held six entries until issue 1206: the two Bedrock cache units were declared here at SERVICE scope, which priced a cache read at $0.00 on eleven different models' behalf from one reason, nine of them with no recorded basis -- and whether a prompt-cache read is chargeable is a property of the model, since AWS prices one on Nova Premier and publishes no such dimension for Claude 3 Haiku in any region. They are now EXPECTED_CACHE_UNIT_OMISSIONS, registered separately, one entry per pricing key and unit. Two ratchets, both in the named test: non-vacuity per member, which derives the metered-unit universe from the writers' own source and the unlisted set from the real pricing file, so an entry that shields nothing fails rather than pre-declaring whatever next carries that name; and a pinned entry count, so a fifth free unit is a deliberate edit with its sourcing reviewed beside it.

lib/idp_common_pkg/pytest.ini::norecurse.turnsOff: pytest collection entirely, for the directories named, in every invocation rooted at lib/idp_common_pkg
lib/idp_common_pkg/pytest.ini::norecurse.reason: One added entry, `manual_tests`, holding operator-run scripts that drive real Bedrock, Athena and DynamoDB against a deployed stack and bill model calls. It is JUDGEMENT because 'these scripts must not run unattended' is a fact about what they do at runtime, not about the tree. What IS computable is checked: the entry shields at least one test_*.py (so it is not dead and pre-exempting), the restated pytest default is complete (setting norecursedirs replaces the default rather than extending it, so dropping `build` or `node_modules` would start walking them), and every directory it hides is also registered in scripts/run_all_tests.py -- without which the exclusion would be recorded in one file and invisible to the test-root guard and docs/testing.md.

predicateConsidered.collects_zero_tests: Does not apply, and its inverse is what matters here. That predicate justifies excluding a directory because pytest finds nothing in it; this exclusion exists because pytest finds five test_*.py modules and must not run them. Asserting zero collection would fail, and asserting non-zero is the non-vacuity ratchet above.

lib/idp_common_pkg/pytest.ini::norecurse.ratchetGap: A new test_*.py added DIRECTLY into an already-registered excluded directory is absorbed silently: the non-vacuity ratchet is already satisfied and the directory is already in QUARANTINE, so nothing fires. A new SUBdirectory does fail, because nesting under a QUARANTINE entry does not inherit the exclusion. Count-pinning would close the residual and is deliberately not used: it would fire on the intended case, an operator adding a sixth script to a directory whose whole purpose is operator scripts.

lib/idp_common_pkg/tests/unit/bedrock/te.memberKind: a `<module path>::<function>` in idp_common that both sleeps and invokes a Bedrock call, and is deliberately not bounded by the invocation budget
lib/idp_common_pkg/tests/unit/bedrock/te.turnsOff: the invocation-budget closure in test_invocation_budget_guard.py for one named function. Without the entry, `test_every_sleeping_bedrock_caller_is_enforced_or_registered` fails on it, which is what it is doing today for its single member.
lib/idp_common_pkg/tests/unit/bedrock/te.reason: One member: rule_validation/z3/rule_translator.py::_invoke_bedrock. It is a real unbounded Bedrock ladder -- 2 application attempts over botocore's defaults at a default 60 s read timeout is nominally 601 s, inside a ConfigurationResolverFunction capped at 120 s -- and it is excluded rather than fixed because bounding it is not the same edit as the other four. Its client is built with `boto3.client("bedrock-runtime")` and NO botocore Config at all, so the fix has to choose a read timeout for work nobody has measured, which is a product decision; and no handler on its call path publishes a deadline, so the gate would be inert there today even if added. Writing a reason that would be false of a second member is the defect this registry exists to catch, so the entry is per function and the module is not exempted. scripts/tests/nested_parameter_defaults_.reason: Discovered as a JSON registry (the `*_baseline.json` glob) and it is one: every member is a finding the gate agrees not to fail on. Whether a given default is the intended value is the judgement, and it is not computable -- a verified defect and a deliberate knob are structurally identical, both being a declared Default no caller overrides. What is computable, and is computed per member, is the FINDING: scripts/tests/nested_parameter_defaults.py derives the set from the templates on every run, so a member cannot be recorded that the tree does not exhibit. The one-reason-per-set failure this registry exists to prevent is addressed inside the file rather than here, because that is where a member lives: each entry carries its own sentence about what reads the parameter and what the default means to it, and test_each_baseline_entry_answers_for_itself fails on an empty one, so every name sharing one sentence about defaults usually being deliberate is a test failure rather than a review question. The file is also not a laundering step: --write refuses to add a member, or to record one whose template has started reading it, without --allow-new-unpassed "<reason>", which is stored in the file -- without that refusal the gate would redden on a newly self-disabled feature, print 'record it or pass it', and --write would record it with nothing attached.

predicateConsidered.not_a_nested_stack_of_parent: It answers the opposite question and would hold for no member here. Every member belongs to a template that template.yaml deploys as an AWS::CloudFormation::Stack -- which is the precondition for being a finding at all, since the scan derives its universe from gate_premises.nested_stack_sources(). A member for which this predicate held could not be in the file.

scripts/tests/nested_parameter_defaults_.ratchetGap: Closure and staleness are both enforced -- a finding in neither section fails, and a recorded member the scan no longer produces fails -- but nothing can check that a member is in the RIGHT section. Moving either known defect into `accepted` with a plausible sentence passes every test here; what it costs is a visible diff on a reasoned entry, which is the control, and it is a review control rather than a gate. The scan is also one level deep: it reads the AWS::CloudFormation::Stack resources of template.yaml, and a nested template declaring one of its own would not be followed. Measured on this tree, none does, so the gap is forward-looking rather than live.

scripts/tests/test_coverage_debt.py::COV.turnsOff: the coverage ratchet's per-file baseline for ONE source file inside a handler directory the fan-out does measure: the file carries no floor, so its coverage is ratcheted at nothing while every sibling in the same directory is held. It does not remove the file from the gate's universe -- the per-file closure derives the unfloored files on every run and compares them against this map as an exact set.
scripts/tests/test_coverage_debt.py::COV.reason: coverage.py's file discovery walks the measured source and recurses into a subdirectory only if that directory is an importable package, so a module below a non-package directory reaches the coverage data only when something imports it -- and a file absent from the report can be given no floor at all. That is a property of the one path, it is computed per member by the predicate named above (bound to the fan-out root the file sits under, because the walk DOES reach a file sitting directly in the measured source whether or not that directory is a package, and a version asking about the parent alone answers 'unreachable' for every handler module in this repository), and it was measured in both directions rather than read off coverage.py: dropping an __init__.py into the directory puts the file in the report at 0.00%. THE RATCHET IS UNIVERSE CLOSURE OVER FILES, which is also why the entry is keyed by path rather than counted. The gate derives the unfloored source files under every measured fan-out root on each run and compares them against this map as an exact set, so a member in neither the baseline nor here fails by name. The first version pinned the cardinality, and a cardinality pin passes when the audited file is replaced -- demonstrated, by deleting this file and planting an unreachable module under a different root, which left a different source file shipping unmeasured with the gate green. The comparison is now an exact set, so BOTH directions fail: an unaccounted file, and a stale entry whose file has gained a floor or been deleted, which would otherwise pre-exempt whatever next occupies the path. The predicate deliberately does not claim that nothing imports the file -- a module below a non-package directory that something does import is discovered and measurable, so the exemption would be unsound -- and the gate supplies that half by deriving membership from the files with no recorded floor rather than from the filesystem. The remedy for the one member is in the tree rather than here: make the directory a package, or have a test import the module.

Multi-Doc Discovery needs a multimodal embedding model, the preset's own comment records that GovCloud offered none when it was checked, the setting has no enable flag the preset could turn off, and pinning an id nobody has confirmed with a Converse call would contradict the preset header. So the preset leaves the system default in place and says so. test_each_exempt_value_is_still_needed fails when the merged value at the path is no longer the excused one, so the entry goes stale the moment the default or the preset changes rather than excusing whatever lands there next.

scripts/tests/test_classification_flat_k.turnsOff: nothing. It is the universe the two parametrised tests beside it are driven over, so a member being in it is what makes that member asserted about rather than what excuses it. Both tests require the value to be ANSWERED rather than to raise -- _is_page_limit truncates, and int(inf) raises OverflowError while int(nan) raises ValueError -- and the second requires FileShapeConfig to normalise the same value to 'ALL', so the two predicates are pinned to agree about it.
scripts/tests/test_classification_flat_k.reason: Discovered through the name route, on the NON_ fragment, and it is not a carve-out: these three values are the cases the shared parity table in src/ui/src/utils/__tests__/page-limit.fixtures.json cannot carry, because JSON has no spelling for Infinity or NaN. Registered rather than renamed, since renaming a constant to slip past discovery is the failure this registry exists to prevent and 'not an exemption at all' is a decision it is built to record. The closure is what makes the split safe and it is asserted rather than assumed, in test_no_float_spelling_is_unaccounted_for_by_both_case_sets: every member here is non-finite so none belongs in the table, nothing in the table is non-finite so none belongs here, and math.isfinite partitions float on exactly inf, -inf and nan, which is why three is all of them. No per-member fact is computed because there is none to compute -- which float spellings Python calls non-finite is a property of the language. What a reviewer should check instead is that the assertions are real: remove the math.isfinite guard from _is_page_limit and all three cases go red, which is how the guard was verified when it was written.
